Forge v0.5.0-preview.1 is the first multi-session CLI preview. Install it explicitly through npm `next`; stable `latest` remains unchanged.

## Highlights

- Open independent TUI conversations with Ctrl+N; use Ctrl+P to switch between live and saved sessions while background tasks continue.
- Run two tasks by default, queue up to 32 more in FIFO order, and configure 1–16 concurrent tasks with FORGE_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS.
- Keep drafts, model selections, output, approvals and cancellation scoped to each session. /exit cancels all workbench tasks and waits for execution and persistence.
- Create separate Git branches/worktrees from HEAD for new sessions. Uncommitted files, ignored files and dependencies are not copied. Non-Git sessions retain their directory and its execution lease.
- Delete saved chats without deleting workspace files. Close an idle view with x before requesting saved-history deletion with Ctrl+D; y confirms, Enter/Escape cancels.

## Install

Node.js 24.22.1 or newer is required.

```bash
npm install --global @jslee124/forge@next
# Reproducible exact version:
npm install --global @jslee124/forge@0.5.0-preview.1
forge --version
```

Existing stable installs are not moved to this preview automatically. Restart Forge after upgrading. See [sessions](https://github.com/jslee124/forge/blob/v0.5.0-preview.1/docs/product/reference/SESSIONS.md) and [TUI controls](https://github.com/jslee124/forge/blob/v0.5.0-preview.1/docs/product/reference/CLI_UI.md).

## Verification

The feature commit passed 899 local tests (6 opt-in skips), 223 deterministic checks, source/type/docs checks and packed-install verification. Real DeepSeek TUI and macOS Electron development flows were tested. Electron Codex used gpt-6-luna with low effort and confirmed an interrupted turn without stopping another session. The immutable-tag workflow runs its own release checks before publication. See [release evidence](https://github.com/jslee124/forge/blob/main/evals/reports/v0.5.0-preview.1/README.md).

This is a preview. Live Codex TUI, multi-turn Codex recovery, long-running load, Windows/Linux TUI behavior and broader provider coverage remain unverified. Worktrees do not isolate ports, databases, credentials or external effects. Queues are process-local and are not durable or shared across processes. This npm package does not update Desktop; its separately published release is desktop-0.5.0-preview.1.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jslee124/forge/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0-preview.1
